newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper could break $2,600 on fresh run.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper could break $2,600 on fresh run.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
The copper market is targeting $2,570 initially on its way to breaking $2,600 on Thursday after reaching a one-year high on Wednesday night, analysts said.
Fears over tightening supplies in the coming weeks should ensure spreads remain wide, they added.
COPPER -
The market could build on Wednesday's one-year high and having taken out the $2,570-$2,580 resistance should be on its way to $2,600, analysts said.
The technical indicators are basically favourable, albeit the RSI is creeping up at 73, approaching over-bought, and are backed by a precarious physical supply background.

Threats of force majeure being called at Ok Tedi on Papua New Guinea have added to the tensions created by the ongoing strike at copper-nickel producer Inco's Sudbury, Ontario, mining and refining complex.
Russia's copper-nickel producer Norilsk is also raising concerns as it faces limited gas supply to fire its refineries.
One broker also said Canadian copper-zinc producer Hudson Bay has potential labour unrest brewing at its Flin Flon, Manitoba, mining-processing complex.

Ok Tedi's problems revolve around low water levels preventing barging copper concentrates from the mine to its Fly River export point and already Nippon Mining and Metals has announced delays to its June smelter feed from the mine.
Ok Tedi could also run out of fuel shortly, forcing it to close.
The additional threats to supply were enough to send prices higher on Wednesday in a market already precariously balanced on historically low stocks and steady offtake.
The backwardation widened on Wednesday to $110 from $60 on Monday, suggesting further volatility, analysts said.

"A good close on the charts allied with a pick up in technical indicators suggests that prices are now capable of pushing towards the top of the current trading channel at $2,650," said Brandeis (Brokers) Ltd in its daily market comment.
At 0745 GMT copper was indicated at $2,581/$2,584 compared with $2,564/$2,568 in late trading on Wednesday.
ALUMINIUM -
A close above Tuesday's levels came after aluminium spent Wednesday in a $9 range, but that was enough to encourage analysts to see further upside for the metal.
Targets are $1,643 and late May's $1,658, although the diffident price pattern suggests a correction cannot be dismissed, they said.

A stock draw on Wednesday and technical indicators turning up -- including the bottoming of the 10-day moving average around $1,605 -- supports the bullish view now that $1,620 resistance has been overcome.
At 0755 GMT aluminium was indicated at $1,623/$1,626, a couple of dollars above Wednesday's late trading level.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
